- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above peak for next 3–7 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling >1% from peak), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until trend reverses.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values if sentiment is neutral or mixed.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 1.00, 0.00, 1.00), model may misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 3–5 days for correction.
